answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks by making every identity expensive to create and easy to verify. Each new agent must post a stake, and when it claims a reputation, a verifier checks the proof against a shared atlas of prior signed work. Flooding a thousand fake agents would cost a thousand stakes, and any one of them that misbehaves can be slashed at once. A single verified crystal of honest history becomes the only real target an attacker can reach for, so the honest majority forms a haven that cheap clones cannot enter for free.
